items.title: A gut-local pathway where enteric neurons relay to DRG sensory neurons
items.summary: Reports an enteric-to-DRG sensory pathway in the mouse gut that contributes to interoception and visceral pain — enteric nervous system neurons relaying signals to spinal (DRG) afferents, rather than DRG endings sensing the gut wall alone.
items.whyItMatters: Squarely your lab's territory: it adds an enteric→DRG link to the gut-sensing story, and cites the Wolfson 2023 colon paper. A fresh model for how DRG afferents fit into gut circuits.

items.title: A current map of the sensory nerves connecting gut to brain
items.citation: Spencer, Hibberd & Hu, 2026, Nature Reviews Gastroenterology & Hepatology
items.summary: A review of the extrinsic sensory nerves that innervate the GI tract — vagal and spinal (DRG) afferents — covering their ending types and the mechanisms that activate them.
items.whyItMatters: A up-to-date orientation to the vagal-vs-DRG sensory landscape your lab works in, and a dense source of recent references.

items.title: Reframing the DRG as a sensory-immune organ, not a passive relay
items.citation: Roger et al., 2026, Annual Review of Neuroscience
items.summary: Argues the dorsal root ganglion is a specialized sensory-immune organ: a macrophage-guarded blood-DRG barrier, neuron-glia microdomains that set sensory gain, and immune signaling that shapes pain and recovery.
items.whyItMatters: Bridges your sensory and neuroimmune interests — the ganglion you study is also an immune compartment, directly relevant to inflammation and pain models.
